subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should `channels.discord.actions.messages` become a backward-compatible boolean-or-object permission group, or should Discord expose separate permanent top-level message-action gates?
rationale: This is a shipped, security-sensitive configuration contract; maintainers must choose its stable shape, default inheritance, and upgrade behavior before implementation can safely proceed.

options.title: Boolean-or-object group
options.body: Keep the shipped boolean as the group default and allow optional send, read, edit, and delete overrides beneath `messages`.

options.title: Separate top-level gates
options.body: Add independent message-action booleans and explicitly define how they override or supersede the existing `messages` group.

options.title: Keep coarse gate
options.body: Retain the current grouped authorization and document that deployments cannot independently prohibit destructive message actions.

recommendation.title: Boolean-or-object group
recommendation.body: Keep the shipped boolean as the group default and allow optional send, read, edit, and delete overrides beneath `messages`.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository guidance assigns the Discord subsystem to this owner, and the unresolved choice is the permanent Discord configuration contract.
